# Adventure RPG Engine — Editor Manual (LLM index)

> Authoritative guide for answering user questions about how to achieve effects in the
> Adventure RPG Engine editor (a 2D action-RPG maker, SNES/GBA style). When this index is
> not enough, read docs/manual/index.html in full. When the codebase contradicts the
> manual, the code wins (docs/RPG_Spec.md and docs/code_base.md).

## How to use this
The full manual is `index.html` (same folder). It is plain semantic HTML — read it directly.
The most useful section for "how do I…" questions is the numbered recipes (R1–R29).

## Quick recipe map (effect → where in the editor)
- Enemy chases the player → Edit Enemy Types → Hit Reaction & AI → Aggro range > 0  (R1)
- Enemy flies back / immovable when hit → Knockback resist 0..1  (R2)
- Hits stagger an enemy → Hitstun seconds > 0  (R3)
- Projectile bounces off walls (stone) vs breaks (arrow/bullet) → Weapons → On wall hit = Rebound/Break  (R4)
- Enemy shoots projectiles → Edit Enemy Types → add Ranged attack  (R5)
- "Kill N enemies" quest → Quest State variable + enemy Kill counter var + NPC dialogue Condition/Action  (R6)
- NPC says a live variable → put `$Variable_Id` in dialogue, e.g. `You killed $Crows_Killed crows.` Chapter scope wins over universal; IDs are case-sensitive; `$$` is a literal `$`.  (R6/R10)
- Enemies stay dead / respawn → dead within a session; placement respawn flag to bring back; every launch is a new game so they always spawn  (R7)
- Placed enemies don't appear → check waypoint present, typeId matches a type, not walled off (state no longer carries over between launches)  (R8)
- Shop NPC → interaction mode is TYPE-level only (no per-placement override). Edit NPC Types → default interaction = Shop + inventory rows; place an instance (stock can be overridden per instance). Setting a shop stock override on a Talk-type placement does NOT make it a shop.  (R9)
- Branching dialogue / choices → NPC → Edit Instance Dialogue (Start/Dialogue/Choice/Condition/Action/End)  (R10)
- Place a pickup → Items tab to define, then Screens → Edit Items. Enable Respawn when screen reloads for repeatable flowers; leave it off for one-time coins/keys.  (R11)
- Choose playable character / edit sprite → Characters tab → Playable + Edit Sprite  (R12)
- Attack/hurt/death animations → add sprite frames labelled attack_1/cast/hit_react/death/hurt/dead  (R13)
- Add & link a screen → Screens tab directional N/S/E/W controls  (R14)
- Quickly test current screen → Play Selected Screen (fresh launch)  (R15)
- Tune combat feel globally → constants in src/game/engine.cpp (rebuild)  (R16)
- Placed NPC/enemy doesn't appear or react → (1) placement not saved (creating a TYPE places nothing; place an instance + save); (2) sprite id case/name mismatch vs assets/game/sprites/<id>.sprite.json (case-sensitive); (3) NPC interaction is manual (green prompt + press E) and the 24px default radius is small — raise it; shop needs type interaction=Shop; (4) walled off  (R17)
- Animated scenery tile (water/fire/torch) → add region to Tile Palette → "Edit Sprite" on the row → add frames in Sprite editor → Refresh → tile shows "● anim (N)" → Stamp it (active layer = Wall in front / Floor behind). Single-frame tiles stamp static pixels.  (R18)
- Weapon pickup shows wrong/no sprite on map → pick the weapon in Edit Items; it auto-fills the on-map pickup sprite from the weapon sprite (separate from the weapon's own sprite).  (R19)
- Slingshot/bow won't use ammo → ammo lives in the INVENTORY (shown in an "AMMO" section), fired directly; weapon ammoTypeId must match an Ammo item id/targetId. No separate ammo pool.  (R20)
- Editor opens last project automatically (projects/.editor_session); Project Manager opens/creates/deletes projects. Creating or opening ensures the complete declared assets/raw and assets/game folder tree, including sfx/doors and sfx/walking; chapters get dialogue/<chapter-id>.  (R21)
- Obstacles / hazards → Screens → Edit Screen Graphics → Map Logic; add Spike/Pit/Timed Spike rectangles, set tile position/size, optional sprite id, and timed spike cycle fields. Obstacles do not have a top-level tab.  (R22)
- Door behavior overview → Screens → Edit Doors; Free Use+target transfers, Locked is permanent, Requires Item+target transfers, Requires Item without target unlocks in place. Required Item uses the key item ID, not Target. Door sprites draw above the Wall layer so a doorway carved into wall art stays visible.  (R23)
- Linked screen doors → set a door's Target screen and explicit Target Tile X/Y spawn, then Apply (or "Link / create paired door"). The editor auto-creates a matching paired door at the centre of the target screen and links both via targetDoorId; use "Set Spawn Tile On Target Screen" to click the arrival tile. (.admap is v11.)  (R30)
- NPC/enemy enters, speaks, or leaves on a path → edit its path/spline; use off-screen X/Y coordinates, Enter/Speak/Leave waypoint actions, and Speech time.  (R24)
- Draw a polygon in a sprite → Sprite editor → Polygon; click vertices, double-click/Enter to close, right-click/Esc to cancel. Reorder frames by dragging thumbnails or Earlier/Later.  (R25)
- Choose paint/sprite colors → Screen Graphics and Sprite editor use the fixed 128-color Atari 2600 NTSC palette. Screen Graphics also has Transparent; Sprite palette swatches can be replaced and Add color opens the same selector. Existing legacy colors are preserved until replaced.
- Destination door → set Target screen ID, set Target Tile X/Y with the point-and-click spawn picker, and Apply; a paired door is auto-created on the target screen for the return link. Optionally require/consume a key.  (R26/R30)
- Same-screen key barrier → Requires Item + key item ID + empty Target screen; unlock persists and an unanimated door disappears when crossed.  (R27)
- Door SFX → put `.wav`/`.ogg` under assets/game/sfx/doors and select Open, Close, Locked dropdowns.  (R28)
- Walking SFX → put `.wav`/`.ogg` under assets/game/sfx/walking and choose it from Screens → Edit Music/SFX. The loop plays only while the player is moving on that screen.
- Audio: only one screen-music track is active per game process. Changing tracks stops the previous music first; one-shot SFX and walking loops still mix over the active track.
- Repeatable flowers vs one-time coins → Edit Items → Respawn when screen reloads checked/unchecked; placement IDs must be unique.  (R29)

## Key concepts
- Tiles 16x16, screens 48x32 tiles. Chapters = grids of linked screens.
- Reusable assets live in project.adgame; dialogue trees are chapter-scoped.
- Game state registry: named ints/bools/items; quests, kills, money, dialogue all route through it.
  Variable names are designer-authored, never hard-coded. Money = integer var "Money".
- Dialogue interpolation: `$Variable_Id` displays live integer or boolean state in dialogue, choices, speaker text, fallback lines, and timed speech. Use `${Variable.With-Dots}` for IDs containing dots/hyphens. Chapter-scoped values take precedence; unknown placeholders remain visible; `$$` escapes `$`.
- Persistence: defeated enemies + state tracked in-memory within a session and written to save.adstate, but every launch starts a NEW game (state initialized from project defaults); save.adstate is only re-loaded with the --continue launch flag. --fresh test launches also ignore it and don't write.
- Ammo: stored in the inventory (not a separate pool); ranged weapons consume the matching Ammo item directly. Inventory has an AMMO section (sprite + count).
- Tiles: Tile Palette entries can be linked to a sprite (Edit Sprite); a tile whose sprite has >=2 frames is "animated" and stamps as a runtime AnimatedTilePlacement instead of baking pixels. Floor and Overlay bands each have Stack 1-3; higher stacks draw later. Stamping/right-click replaces/removes only the selected slot, while Tile Erase removes all stacks at the cell.
- Screen Graphics placement: while pasting a copied selection or using Stamp, Ctrl+V cycles the mouse reference clockwise through top-left, top-right, bottom-right, and bottom-left. The controls show the active reference, and the canvas ghost marks it in yellow with a Ctrl+V hint.
- Colors: screen graphics and sprite color authoring use the shared 128-color Stella-based Atari 2600 NTSC palette. Sprite documents start with transparent plus all 128 colors in a width-fitting drawing swatch grid (left-click primary, right-click secondary); transparent has a checkerboard/slash marker. The sprite canvas Picker can still sample colors already present in legacy art; loading/saving does not automatically remap old colors.
- Screen Graphics brushes: size range is 1-32. Smudge drags to carry/blend active-layer pixels; Strength controls the blend and every opaque result is quantized to the nearest Atari palette color. Transparent source pixels are skipped. Spray and Dither brush shapes feather toward their edges, including with Smudge.
- Screen Graphics Lighten/Darken: Intensity controls color-change strength; Graduation controls feather width around the brush edge (0% hard edge, 100% graduation across the full radius).
- Runtime collision tiles do not draw a yellow debug overlay. The optional yellow Wall guide exists only in Screen Graphics.
- Screen Graphics animated-tile overlay: clear the "Animated tiles" checkbox to hide existing placement markers while painting Floor/Wall pixels beneath transparent animation frames. This is visibility-only and does not delete placements; the active Stamp ghost remains visible.
- Editor zoom: `=`/keypad `+` zooms in and `-`/keypad `-` zooms out in the Sprite and Screen Graphics editors. Shortcuts are ignored while editing a field.
- Screen Graphics tool shortcuts: B Pencil, E Eraser, D Darken, G Lighten, U Smudge, F Fill, L Line, R Rect, S Select, I Pick; `[`/`]` shrink/grow the brush; Ctrl+Z undo, Ctrl+C/Ctrl+V copy/paste, Esc clears a selection. Tool buttons show their key on hover; single-key shortcuts only fire without Ctrl/Cmd and not while a field is focused.
- Sprite resize: the Resize dialog accepts either pixels ("Dimensions (px)") or whole tiles ("Size in tiles", 1 tile = 16px); the fields stay in sync. Keep-pixels grows/crops centred art, Scale-pixels rescales all frames/layers (nearest-neighbour).
- Sprite overlays: the "Tiles" toggle overlays brighter tile-boundary lines every 16px (separate from the per-pixel "Grid") to aid drawing accuracy on multi-tile sprites; Pivot and Body guides are also overlay-only. None render in game.
- Projectile size: a fired projectile draws its ammo sprite at the same on-screen size as the ammo pickup (aspect-ratio preserved), so high-resolution ammo art (e.g. a 32x32 slingshot stone) is not oversized in flight.
- Combat: melee has windup→active→recovery; hits cause knockback + hitstun + flash; lethal → dead/fade.
  Projectiles are team-tagged (enemy shots hit the player). Aggro enemies chase then return to nearest path point.

## Runtime controls
Keyboard: Move WASD/arrows; Z melee; X ranged; E interact/confirm/use; I inventory; Esc display menu; F11 toggle 2x fullscreen.
Gamepad: D-pad/left stick move; South (A) interact; West (X) melee; East (B) ranged; bumpers cycle aim; North (Y)/Start inventory; Select/Back opens the display menu (same as Esc).

## Runtime display
The game uses a 768x540 logical canvas (768x512 playfield plus 28px HUD), centred integer scaling, and black letterboxing. The playfield scales to the largest whole-number multiple that fits the window, so enlarging the window enlarges the play area in crisp integer steps (never stretched). Escape (or gamepad Select/Back) opens Windowed 1x, Windowed 2x, Fullscreen 2x, and Quit Game. Fullscreen 2x presents a 1536x1080 image without stretching.
